evidence.intree_statement: Program Definition Proset {A : Type} {R : relation A} (P : PreOrder R) : Category := {| obj := A; hom := R; homset := fun A B => {| Setoid.equiv := fun _ _ => True |}; id := fun x => reflexivity ...; compose := fun x y z f g => transitivity ... |}  (header: identities from reflexivity, composition from transitivity; 'The resulting category is "thin": any two parallel morphisms are equal')

Program Instance hom_preorder {C : Category} : PreOrder (@hom C) := { PreOrder_Reflexive := fun _ => id; PreOrder_Transitive := fun _ _ _ f g => g ∘ f }  (comment: 'the standard observation that a category has an underlying preorder of objects (a preorder is exactly a thin category)')
Definition LessThanEqualTo_Category : Category := @Proset nat PeanoNat.Nat.le PeanoNat.Nat.le_preorder

statement_record.book: A preorder is a category with at most one arrow p -> p'; defining p <= p' iff an arrow p -> p' exists yields a reflexive (identities) and transitive (composition) relation on objects; conversely any set with a reflexive transitive relation determines such a category, arrows being exactly the pairs p <= p'. This is a bijective correspondence between preordered sets and such categories.
statement_record.intree: Proset: any PreOrder R on A yields the category with obj := A, hom := R, all parallel arrows identified (thin by construction); hom_preorder: every category carries the preorder on objects with reflexivity id and transitivity composition.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: both single directions are present and faithful (thinness realized setoid-style by declaring all parallel morphisms equal, and hom_preorder even applies to an arbitrary category, of which the thin case is the book's converse), but the bijective correspondence itself is nowhere stated as a theorem.

gap: The round-trip/bijection between preordered sets and thin categories is not formalized: there is no thinness predicate on categories in-tree, and no theorem that Proset and hom_preorder are mutually inverse (that Proset (hom_preorder C) recovers a thin C up to isomorphism, and that hom_preorder (Proset P) is P).
